decisions.reason: The refined height and quiet visual role of the second V do not change the É accent's literal derivation, geometry, or peak-alignment rules.

The source message separately modifies this Requirement's proprietary-alphabet rule, and that same-message MODIFY is already complete; the second-V hierarchy introduces no additional change to the remaining letterforms.
The second V's revised height and supporting role leave the approved Hero V geometry and master-foundation status unchanged.

The candidate's general composition and visual-hierarchy rules remain valid; the more precise second-V height and echo behavior belong to the atomic second-V Requirement and do not make any composition attribute stale.
The source changes the second V's height hierarchy and prominence, not its shared terminal gesture or terminal construction.
The second V's visual hierarchy does not alter the deferred champagne-metal material treatment, material sequence, or shared material language.
Describing the second V as a quiet, non-competing echo is consistent with the existing brand-expression principles but does not change their current state.
The refinement of the second V does not affect the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
The second V design refinement does not change the obligation to deliver final production-ready artwork.
